newsitem.title: USA: Hilton CEO sticks to $55/shr offer for ITT.
newsitem.headline: Hilton CEO sticks to $55/shr offer for ITT.

text.p: Hilton Hotels Corp Chief Executive Officer Stephen Bollenbach said Tuesday Hilton would not consider raising its $55-a-share bid for ITT Corp unless it met with ITT management and decided the company was worth more.
He also said in a teleconference that any higher bid would have to meet Hilton's goal of ensuring the deal is accretive to earnings.
"I don't think we need to change the price unless we meet with ITT," Bollenbach said.
He said he would consider a higher price only if, after meeting with ITT executives, Hilton determined ITT had greater value.
Shares of ITT were up 14-3/4 at 57-3/8 at midday. Hilton shares were up three points at 28-1/4.
Bollenbach saw the stock action as evidence that Hilton's bid was in the right ballpark and that investors buying the stock would likely support the deal.
"You know where those shares are going...they are going to people who want to vote for this transaction," he said.

One of Hilton's primary goals in gaining ownership of ITT's large, full-service Sheraton hotels, he said. Hilton would consider changing the brand names of some large Sheraton hotels to Hilton where operations overlap.
ITT's hotel and casino operations run under the Caesars World brand would likely remain unchanged, he said.
"It gives us another brand name," Arthur Goldberg, president of Hilton's gaming operations, said in the conference call.
He added, "Caesar's should have expanded beyond Atlantic City and Las Vegas a long time ago."
He does not see any overlap in Atlantic City between Hilton and Caesars.
In Las Vegas, Hilton's casino, themed after the city of Paris, will continue on track for development, Goldberg said.

Bollenbach said Hilton would review ITT's $3.0 billion expansion plan, which includes new hotel rooms at Caesars Palace and renovation of the Sheraton Desert Inn in Las Vegas, as well as building casinos in conjunction with themed restaurant chain Planet Hollywood International Inc.
He declined to say which plans, if any, would be put on hold.

He also declined to speculate on the fate of entertainment assets held by ITT's MSG L.P. unit. He labeled those assets, including Madison Square Garden in New York and two professional sports teams, as non-core to Hilton's business.

Bollenbach said he did not believe Hilton's debt ratings would be hurt by the deal. "This will in no way adversely impact our credit rating," he said. "It's very important that we maintain an investment grade rating."
Moody's Investors Service Inc is reviewing the ratings of both Hilton and ITT for possible downgrade, and Standard & Poor's Corp has both ratings on CreditWatch with negative implications.
Hilton Chief Financial Officer Matthew Hart said Hilton's goal for maintaing its debt ratings is to generate cash that is four times as great as its interest expense.
He said Hilton would be able to maintain that "four times" ratio after the ITT acquisition.
Hart said many of Hilton's bankers are "very supportive of the transaction."
Bollenbach said he did not see Nevada gaming regulations as a stumbling block to an ITT deal.
